newsitem.title: USA: US House strikes $91 mln in FDA drug user fees.
newsitem.headline: US House strikes $91 mln in FDA drug user fees.

text.p: The U.S. House struck from a fiscal 1998 appropriations bill on Thursday a direction to the Food and Drug Adminstration to collect $91 million in prescription drug user fees.

Representative Richard Burr, North Carolina, asked for a parliamentary ruling that the mandate was out of order on the funding bill. The presiding officer of the House agreed and ordered the seven lines of instructions to be struck from the bill.
Burr was not immediately available to explain his challenge of the user fees, which are paid by pharmacuetical firms to underwrite FDA reviews of drugs, nor was a spokeswoman for Burr.
Earlier in the day, the Senate passed an appropriations bill that included the $91 million in user fees, so the issue may be addressed when the two chambers write a final version of the bill.
